title: Dissociation and flow cytometric isolation of murine intestinal epithelial cells
author: Ge, Zadeh, et al.
materials: LIVE/DEAD Fixable Violet Dead Cell Stain Kit

Timing: (20 min per sample)
18.Acquire samples on FACS machine and sort cells into post-sort buffer.
Note: For our studies, we used SH800S cell sorter (Sony, Japan) and CytoFlex SRT cell sorter (Beckman Coulter, USA) and analyzed the data using FlowJo software package (Tree Star, USA).
19.Mix cells with AOPI staining solution at 1:1 ratio; Load 20 μL onto slide and count using Auto 2000. Adjust volume to obtain the required cell recovery target.
Alternatives: Cells can also be counted using a hemocytometer.
Note: The actual number of cells is about 65%–80% of counts recorded by cell sorter.
20.After cell counting, immediately proceed to downstream analysis:a.If cells are used for bulk RNA-seq, spin down the cells at 500 g and 4°C for 5 min and carefully remove supernatant by pipetting; resuspend cell pellets in 350 μL of Buffer RLT Plus supplemented with 1% β-mercaptoethanol.Pause point: samples can be stored at −80°C for months until being further processed for RNA isolation using RNeasy Micro Plus kit (https://www.qiagen.com/us/products/discovery-and-translational-research/dna-rna-purification/rna-purification/total-rna/rneasy-plus-kits/).CRITICAL: Removal of supernatants as much as possible is crucial for ensuring efficient cell lysis. We normally keep less than 20 μL of supernatants in the tube so that the cell pellets are not disturbed.CRITICAL: Wear a mask when handling β-mercaptoethanol.b.If cells are used for single-cell RNA-seq, immediately proceed to GEM generation and barcoding (https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/single-cell-immune-profiling/documentation/steps/library-prep/chromium-single-cell-5-reagent-kits-user-guide-v-2-chemistry-dual-index).c.If cells are used for metabolomic analysis, spin down the cells at 500 g and 4°C for 5 min and carefully remove supernatant by pipetting; resuspend cell pellets in1 mL cold DPBS and transfer to 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube for washing. Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 500 g and 4°C for 5 min; completely remove the supernatants.Pause point: Cells can be snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen or on dry ice and store at −80°C for months until metabolite extraction.

steps.title: Prepare buffers and equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare EDTA, FACS, MACS, and post‑sort buffers as described, store them at 4 °C or on ice, and equilibrate a centrifuge compatible with 15 mL and 50 mL Falcon tubes to 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare EDTA buffer.
Prepare FACS buffer.
Prepare MACS buffer.
Prepare post‑sort buffer.
Store all buffers at 4 °C or on ice.
Equilibrate centrifuge to 4 °C for 15 mL and 50 mL tubes.

steps.title: Wash intestinal tissue
steps.instruction: Wash the harvested ileum three times with cold DPBS.

substeps.instruction: Pour out existing DPBS.
Add 10 mL cold DPBS and shake tube up‑and‑down for 20–30 s.
Repeat the addition, shaking, and removal two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Slice tissue into fragments
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue to a petri dish and cut it into small fragments roughly 2–3 cm in length.

steps.title: EDTA incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate tissue fragments in cold EDTA buffer on ice with intermittent shaking.

substeps.instruction: Place fragments into a 15 mL Falcon tube pre‑filled with 7 mL cold EDTA buffer and keep on ice.
Hand‑shake the tube up‑and‑down ~60 cycles (≈0.5 s per cycle) every 7–8 min for a total of 30 min.
After 30 min, shake the tube vigorously for 2 min.
Remove the tissue pieces with tweezers.

steps.title: Wash cells post‑EDTA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge and wash the released cells with cold DPBS.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 500 g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 10 mL cold DPBS to the pellet.

steps.title: TrypLE dissociation
steps.instruction: Digest cell aggregates with TrypLE Express Enzyme at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Spin the cells down at 500 g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant completely.
Add 2 mL TrypLE Express Enzyme and gently resuspend the pellet with 1 mL pipette tips.
Incubate at 22–25 °C for 10 min, pipetting up/down 10 times with 1 mL tips every 3–4 min to break aggregates.

steps.title: Filter cell suspension
steps.instruction: Pass the dissociated cells through a 70 µm cell strainer and wash the strainer.

substeps.instruction: Fill the tube with 10 mL cold DPBS and push the suspension through a 70 µm strainer placed in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Add another 10 mL cold DPBS to wash the strainer.
Collect all flow‑through as a single‑cell suspension.

steps.title: Pellet cells for staining
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension to obtain a cell pellet.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 500 g, 4 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Live/Dead staining
steps.instruction: Stain cells with Live/Dead solution on ice.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL Live/Dead staining solution (1:1000 dilution in DPBS).
Transfer to a FACS tube.
Incubate at 4 °C for 20 min.
Add 4 mL cold DPBS directly to the tube.
Spin down and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: FcR blocking
steps.instruction: Block Fc receptors before antibody staining.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 µL FcR blocking reagent (1:50 dilution in FACS buffer) to resuspend the pellet.
Incubate at 4 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Surface antibody staining
steps.instruction: Stain cells with a cocktail of surface antibodies on ice.

substeps.instruction: Dilute anti‑CD45, anti‑CD31, anti‑TER‑119, and anti‑EpCAM 1:50 in FACS buffer.
Combine the diluted antibodies to make a cocktail.
Add 300 µL of the cocktail to the tube (final 1:100 dilution).
Gently vortex to mix.
Incubate at 4 °C for 30 min.
Add 4 mL cold FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 500 g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 300 µL MACS buffer.
Transfer to FACS tubes equipped with a 35 µm cell‑strainer cap.
Keep the tubes on ice (if cells do not pass through the cap by gravity, a brief centrifugation step may be applied).

steps.title: Acquire and sort cells
steps.instruction: Run the samples on a FACS sorter and collect epithelial cells into post‑sort buffer.

substeps.instruction: Acquire data on the sorter (e.g., SH800S or CytoFlex SRT).
Sort the gated epithelial population into post‑sort buffer.

steps.title: Count sorted cells
steps.instruction: Determine cell number using AOPI staining.

substeps.instruction: Mix the sorted cells 1:1 with AOPI staining solution.
Load 20 µL of the mixture onto a counting slide.
Count cells using an Auto 2000 cell counter (or a hemocytometer as an alternative).
Adjust the final volume to reach the desired cell recovery (actual recovery ≈65–80 % of sorter count).

steps.title: Downstream processing
steps.instruction: Prepare sorted cells for the intended downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Bulk RNA‑seq: Spin at 500 g, 4 °C for 5 min; remove supernatant leaving <20 µL; resuspend pellet in 350 µL Buffer RLT Plus supplemented with 1 % β‑mercaptoethanol; samples may be stored at –80 °C.
Single‑cell RNA‑seq: Proceed directly to GEM generation and barcoding according to the 10x Genomics Chromium protocol.

Metabolomics: Spin at 500 g, 4 °C for 5 min; remove supernatant; resuspend pellet in 1 mL cold DPBS; transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube; centrifuge again at 500 g, 4 °C for 5 min; discard all supernatant; snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen or on dry ice and store at –80 °C.
